For Account Teams pulling assets into a pursuit, the .docx is the editable source of truth; the .html is what gets shared via Teams / SharePoint / client-facing portals.

Key Takeaways

  • The APEX Service Walkthrough is the canonical six-chain-link document (Scenario → Solution → Use Case → Service → Persona → KPI) plus front matter (reference moment · why now) and back matter (wave projection · commercial envelope).
  • Three reference walkthroughs anchor the format: RC-E2E-03 Kroger (cold-chain markdown · 5-agent), RC-E2E-03 MVP Apparel (Friday-Monday WBR · 6-agent), TMT-TEL-RAA-04 Tier-1 Telco (Day-1 → Day-5 close · 6-agent · self-funding).
  • Every walkthrough opens with a concrete reference moment (time, place, event) and three operator-shaped questions the rest of the document answers.
  • Six patterns repeat across all three walkthroughs — concrete reference moment, three questions, five forces, segment portability table, T+0/T+5/T+10 hand-off chain, scope-included / scope-excluded lists with Wave-2 phase-in labels.
  • The TMT-TEL-RAA-04 walkthrough is the only one with self-funding commercial posture — the recovery underwrites the Wave-2 envelope.
  • Folder convention: deliverables/Services/<SERVICE-CODE>_<name>/Tier0-Foundation/ · .docx editable source + .html share-able copy.

Seller Actions

  1. Read all three reference walkthroughs end-to-end before authoring your first.
  2. Copy the §1 reference-moment pattern verbatim — name the time, place, system, and observable signal.
  3. Build the §2.2 "why this segment is the reference" portability table with named portfolio accounts your Account Team can recognise.
  4. Treat §3.4 scope-included / scope-excluded as the section the Practice lead reviews most — make Wave-2 phase-in labels explicit.
  5. Validate the §10 commercial envelope against the audit-firm pre-clearance posture before sharing externally.

This chapter is anchored to the Toyota one-pager at Industries/Automotive/Toyota/01_account/one_pager/Toyota_AgenticAI_OnePager.html. The folder also contains Toyota_OnePager.html (Account Snapshot), Toyota_GTM_OnePager.html (Go-To-Market), a services/ subfolder with one-pagers per Service (Connected-Factory-01, QMS-02, Supply-04, Supply-07, Ops-03), and a bundles/ subfolder with cross-service bundles (B2B-MFG, B2B-SUPP, B2C-AI, B2C-CV, B2C-WARR). The pattern is reusable across every named account in the trilogy.

15B.1 Why a One-Pager — And Why This One-Pager Format

The CIO/CDO conversation that opens an APEX pursuit has three constraints sellers regularly underestimate:

  • The conversation is 30 minutes and the executive will give it 5 minutes of pre-read attention.
  • The leave-behind goes to people who weren't in the room — the executive forwards it to a direct report, who forwards it to a procurement lead, who forwards it to an Account Team partner.
  • The artifact has to print on A4 landscape in a single page that survives screen-share, PDF email, and physical printout without breaking the layout.

The APEX one-pager solves all three by being a single HTML page (1440px wide, A4-landscape print-ready) with three columns (Client context · APEX scenarios → KPI · Recommended approach & funding) and a top navigation bar that lets the reader drill into the Account Snapshot, the Agentic-AI view, the Go-To-Market view, and per-service detail pages.

15B.2 The Eight-Step Recipe

A working seller with the xlsx open, 30 minutes of public-source client research, and a clear named Practice can produce a first draft of the three-page set in 6–8 hours. The recipe:

Step 1 · Identify the client's Practice and primary functional area

The client's Practice determines which sheet of the xlsx you draw scenarios from, and the primary functional area ranks the scenario candidates. Practice mapping is straightforward — automotive OEMs and suppliers → AXLE, grocery/apparel/CPG → RC, payer/provider/life-sciences → HLS, etc. (per Ch 9–15).

Functional area requires reading the client's most recent earnings call, investor day, or annual report and ranking the executive-named priorities against the xlsx's functional-domain taxonomy. The Toyota one-pager ranks Operations·1, Quality·2, Supply Chain·3, Engineering·4 because Sato's FY26 earnings call (the ¥1.45T tariff hit, the certification fallout, the Arene OS launch) maps to exactly those four domains in that order.

Best Practice — let the executive's own words rank the heatmap

Sellers tend to rank functional areas by where APEX has the deepest service catalog (i.e., where we are strong). The Toyota one-pager ranks them by what the executive said in the last public statement. The discipline is to let the executive's words rank the chips and then check whether APEX's catalog covers the top 3–4 — if it does, lead with those; if it doesn't, the pursuit is not yet qualified.

Step 2 · Pull 5–7 candidate scenarios from the xlsx

Open APEX-Scenario-Chains.xlsx. Filter the Scenario Library sheet by the client's Practice prefix (AXLE, RC, HLS, ER, TMT, TH, ICE). Sort by Featured? column descending (Featured rows first), then by Domain matching the top 2–3 functional areas from Step 1.

Pick 5–7 scenarios — typically 3–5 featured chains (★ scenarios with full Scenario → KPI authored) plus 1–2 catalog scenarios that are not yet featured but materially address a client priority. The Toyota example picks 6 from AXLE: 4 from Quality (QMS-02), 1 from Supply (Supply-04), 1 from Operations (Ops-03). All 6 are ⭐ featured.

XLSX → one-pager · scenario picking template
Scenario Library filters (in priority order):
  1. Service Code starts with <Practice prefix>
  2. Featured? == 'Featured'
  3. Domain in <top 3 functional areas from Step 1>
  4. Cap at 7 rows total
  5. Hand-edit to ensure breadth across 3+ Services (not all from one Service)

Per-row data to extract for the one-pager:
  - Title           → "Scenario (the moment)" column in the one-pager table
  - Domain          → "Functional Domain" column (with tag-feat color coding)
  - Service Code    → "Service Code" column (with hyperlink to services/<code>.html)
  - Schemas         → "Schemas" column (compact form, e.g., "QEML+AAML")
  - KPI / Outcome   → "KPI Lift" column (green-highlighted)
  - Brief           → modal pop-up "The Moment" body

Step 3 · Build the headline-scenario chain row

Pick one scenario from Step 2 as the headline — the one most directly tied to the client's named executive priority and the one with the most compelling KPI. Walk that scenario through the five chain cells in the center-column "Service Chain → KPI" panel:

Chain cellSource in xlsxToyota example (headline = First-pass-yield improvement)
Scenario (the moment)Scenario Library.Title + .Brief"FPY drift on a critical sub-assembly correlated with operator-shift × torque-tool calibration interaction."
Solution / AgentFeatured Chains.Solution column · or hand-author from the productized service"FPY-drift agent (ORCH-03) decomposes variance into operator × tool × material × time interactions. HITL on counter-measure scope."
Service (Deloitte)Scenario Library.Service CodeAXLE-QMS-02
Persona (HITL)Featured Chains.Persona column · or hand-author from the productized serviceQuality Director
KPI OutcomeScenario Library.KPI / OutcomeFPY +3–6 pts

Below the chain row, write a one-line aggregate KPI sentence that fuses the headline KPI with the KPIs from the other 5 scenarios — the Toyota line is "Aggregate across all 6 scenarios: FPY +3–6 pts · IATF audit findings −50% · EC effectivity defect −80% · Bottleneck +12–18%". This is the line the executive remembers.

Step 4 · Author the left-column client context

The left column is half data, half story. The data is public — earnings, employee count, geography. The story is the five CEO priorities. Each priority is one sentence in this shape:

CEO priority · canonical sentence shape
<Priority name> — <specific number from earnings call> ; <named executive action>.

Toyota example #1:
  Tariff burden — FY26 OP-income hit ¥1.45T (~$9.7B); ¥1.20T already
  absorbed in 9M FY26; forecast cut to ¥3.80T.

Toyota example #3:
  Arene OS goes live — World premiere on RAV4 May 2025; Woven by Toyota
  uses Azure OpenAI to automate ~80% of code-safety fixes.

Five priorities, five named numbers, five executive-attributable actions. The reader can verify each one against a public source. No marketing language; no aspirational claims. This is the section the CFO reads first and the section that earns the rest of the page its credibility.

Step 5 · Author the right-column recommended approach & funding

The right column is canonical across every client one-pager — only the timeline phasing changes. Three blocks:

  • Recommended approach (W1 / W2 / W3). W1 = 16 weeks, Bronze→Silver→Gold on 1 scenario · W2 = 6–9 months, multi-scenario, multi-site · W3 = annual, enterprise KPI fusion. The phrasing is reused verbatim across clients; only the per-client scenario count changes.
  • Microsoft platform anchors (per scenario). One line per scenario in the table from Step 2, naming the 2–3 pillars that anchor that scenario (Fabric · Foundry · Copilot · Purview). The Toyota example shows 5 of 6 scenarios anchored by Fabric+Foundry+Purview, with 1 (Throughput bottleneck) anchored by Fabric+Foundry+Copilot — the Copilot anchor signals an operator-facing surface, not just a back-office one.
  • Funding strategy. Four lines · canonical structure: BVA discovery envelope · ECIF POC envelope · Azure Credits production envelope · Co-Sell motion. Toyota envelope is BVA $100–200K · ECIF $250–500K · Azure Credits $100–500K · "Microsoft IP partner-led + Deloitte AXLE managed service."
  • 90-day next steps. Five rows · 2-week / 30 / 45 / 60 / 90-day milestones · each is a single deliverable the seller and the Microsoft Account Team can jointly commit to. The Toyota version: "2 Wks — Confirm Microsoft footprint & AXLE scenario shortlist with CIO/CDO · 30 Days — Deliver AXLE Discovery + KPI baseline workshop · 45 Days — ECIF Foundry agent POC scoping · 60 Days — HITL governance & Purview lineage stand-up · 90 Days — First measurable KPI lift on headline scenario."
Independence — the funding strategy is not a "partnership"

Use the language the Toyota one-pager uses: "Microsoft IP partner-led + Deloitte AXLE managed service." This describes the funding mechanism (Microsoft's IP partner program) and the delivery role (Deloitte's managed-service offering) without implying a Deloitte–Microsoft "partnership" or "alliance." Sellers occasionally drift into "joint go-to-market" or "alliance funding" — both fail Independence review. DMTSP, Microsoft platform capabilities, Microsoft-native deployment are the canonical phrases.

Step 6 · Add the three-layer value view (Frontline · Operational · Executive)

Below the scenarios table, three small cards summarise who feels the value at each organisational layer. The discipline is to write each card in one sentence grounded in the named scenarios above.

Three-layer value view · canonical shape
Frontline — Who Feels It
  <one-sentence operator-shaped outcome>

Operational — Who Runs It
  <one-sentence middle-management outcome>

Executive — Who Sees the Lift
  <one-sentence C-suite outcome that ties to the named priorities in the left column>

Toyota example:
  Frontline: "TPS andon goes from line-stop to agent-led counter-measure
              with operator-skill-aware re-balance."
  Operational: "Quality directors execute IATF audit prep with CAPA-effectiveness
                verified at 90 days; ops managers see takt variance attribution
                within shifts."
  Executive: "Chairman Toyoda sees recurrence-prevention measurable;
              CFO sees tariff offset accelerated through agent-led cost-out
              at supplier interface."

This is the highest-ROI block in the one-pager for the executive read. It is the only place where the operator language, the middle-management language, and the C-suite language sit side-by-side on the same page. It is also the block that wins the most edits in review — author it last, after everything else has settled.

Step 7 · Add scenario drill-in modals (or per-Service detail pages)

Each scenario row in the center-column table opens a modal pop-up with the full chain expanded — "The Moment" / "Solution / Agent" / "Use Case (Wave-2 delivery)" / "Service (productized)" / "Persona & HITL Approver" / "KPI / Outcome" / "Wave Ribbon (W1 · W2 · W3)" / "Featured Chain". The modal content for each scenario draws from the xlsx's Featured Chains sheet.

For higher-fidelity pursuits, replace modals with linked per-Service detail pages in services/<code>.html. The Toyota example uses both — modals for the inline drill-in and services/QMS-02.html, services/Supply-04.html, etc. for the deep-dive pages that the engagement architect hands to the client's technical lead in the follow-up meeting.

Cross-reference: each modal / detail page should link back to the corresponding Service Walkthrough in the engagement deliverables folder (Ch 15A). The walkthrough is the long-form artifact; the one-pager modal is the executive-facing summary.

Step 8 · Print-test on A4 landscape and link from the Account Snapshot

The final discipline step: open the HTML in a browser, hit Print, set page size to A4 landscape, set scale to "Fit to page," and verify nothing breaks. The CSS in the Toyota reference uses @page { size: A4 landscape; margin: 0; } and body { width: 1440px; } plus @media print { body { width: 100% } } — copy this exactly to keep the print behaviour consistent.

Finally, link the one-pager from the Account Snapshot Markdown at 01_account/<Client>_Account_Snapshot.md so the Account Team's day-to-day notes carry a single jump-point into the package. The Toyota snapshot opens with a "Meeting Details / Revenue Influence Summary" header that names the one-pager package as the leave-behind for the next CIO/CDO meeting.

15B.4 Five Anti-Patterns Sellers Make on Their First One-Pager

Anti-patternWhy it failsCorrection
Picking too many scenarios (10+ rows in the center table)Loses the executive's focus; signals the seller doesn't know what to lead withCap at 7; lead with one headline; the rest support the breadth claim, not the depth claim
Marketing language in CEO priorities ("transformative" · "industry-leading")Reads as Deloitte's voice, not the client's; fails the verification testUse the executive's own words from the earnings call; cite numbers; avoid adjectives
Generic recommended approach ("we'll do discovery, then build, then scale")Could apply to any pursuit; signals no client-specific designW1/W2/W3 canonical phrasing is fine; what changes per client is the headline scenario named in W1 and the KPI lift named in W3
Microsoft pillars listed without scenario tieImplies platform-led pitch, not outcome-led; fails the "why MS" testPer-scenario Microsoft pillar mapping (Fabric · Foundry · Copilot · Purview) makes the platform investment outcome-attributable
Funding strategy mentions "partnership"Fails Independence review immediately"Microsoft IP partner-led + Deloitte managed service" is the canonical phrasing. DMTSP. Never partnership.

15B.5 Relationship to the Service Walkthroughs (Ch 15A)

The one-pager and the walkthrough are different artifacts for different moments. The one-pager opens the conversation; the walkthrough deepens it. Sellers should produce them in this order:

StageArtifactAudienceLength
Pre-meeting / discoveryOne-Pager package (this chapter) — Account Snapshot + Agentic AI + GTM + per-Service detail pagesCIO / CDO / CFO / Chief Merchant — and the people they forward it to3 pages + drill-ins
Wave-1 envisioningService Walkthrough (Ch 15A) — one per anchor Service per anchor clientEngagement lead · Practice lead · client technical architect~200 paragraphs · ~35 tables
Wave-2 buildSprint UC catalog (per Service Walkthrough §5) — UC-01 through UC-20 with HITL ladderDelivery PM · engagement architect · client's project lead20 UCs · ~80 pages

The one-pager scenarios in the center table should map 1:1 to flagship chains in Ch 9–15's Practice Service Catalogs and to the reference walkthroughs in Ch 15A. If a one-pager references a scenario that doesn't appear in the xlsx, that's a signal — either the xlsx needs updating, or the scenario isn't yet productized and shouldn't be on the leave-behind.

15B.6 The Template Shortcut

Copy the Toyota folder structure verbatim for a new client, replace the client-specific content per the eight-step recipe, and you have a one-pager package in under a day:

Bash · spin up a new client one-pager from the Toyota template
# 1. Copy the Toyota template to your new client folder
cp -r Industries/Automotive/Toyota/01_account/one_pager \
      Industries/<Practice>/<NewClient>/01_account/

# 2. Rename the three HTML pages to the new client name
cd Industries/<Practice>/<NewClient>/01_account/one_pager/
mv Toyota_OnePager.html              <NewClient>_OnePager.html
mv Toyota_AgenticAI_OnePager.html    <NewClient>_AgenticAI_OnePager.html
mv Toyota_GTM_OnePager.html          <NewClient>_GTM_OnePager.html

# 3. Work through the 8-step recipe inside each HTML page,
#    replacing the Toyota content with the new client's content
#    drawn from APEX-Scenario-Chains.xlsx and 30 min of public research.

# 4. Keep the services/ and bundles/ folder names as-is;
#    rename only the content inside them to match the new client's
#    Practice scenarios (e.g., AXLE-* → RC-E2E-*, HLS-E2E-*, etc.)

Key Takeaways

  • The APEX client one-pager is a three-page HTML package (Account Snapshot · Agentic AI · Go-To-Market) with per-Service detail pages and cross-service bundles — designed for A4 landscape print and forwardable as a single leave-behind.
  • Every one-pager has six structural blocks: Header band · Tagline · Left-column client context · Center-column APEX scenarios · Right-column recommended approach & funding · Footer.
  • The eight-step recipe converts APEX-Scenario-Chains.xlsx into a client-specific Agentic-AI One-Pager in 6–8 hours: identify Practice + functional area · pick 5–7 scenarios · build headline chain · author CEO priorities (executive-attributable, numbers-cited) · canonical W1/W2/W3 approach + BVA/ECIF/Azure-Credits funding · three-layer value view · scenario drill-in modals or per-Service pages · A4 print-test.
  • The Toyota Agentic-AI One-Pager is the worked reference example — 6 AXLE scenarios spanning Quality (4), Supply (1), and Operations (1), anchored against Sato's FY26 earnings call (tariff burden, Arene OS, certification fallout).
  • The one-pager opens the conversation; the Service Walkthrough (Ch 15A) deepens it. Scenarios on the one-pager must map 1:1 to flagship chains in the Practice Service Catalogs (Ch 9–15) and to walkthroughs in the engagement deliverables folder.
  • Five anti-patterns to avoid: too many scenarios, marketing language in CEO priorities, generic recommended approach, Microsoft pillars without scenario tie, "partnership" language in funding.

Seller Actions

  1. Open the Toyota reference one-pager (Industries/Automotive/Toyota/01_account/one_pager/Toyota_AgenticAI_OnePager.html) and read it end-to-end before authoring your first.
  2. For your next pursuit, identify the client's Practice (Ch 9–15) and rank functional areas from the executive's most recent public statement, not from where APEX is strongest.
  3. Filter APEX-Scenario-Chains.xlsx · Scenario Library sheet by Practice prefix + Featured + top functional domains; export 5–7 candidate scenarios.
  4. Author the 5 CEO priorities first — they earn the rest of the page its credibility; sellers who skip this end up with a generic deck dressed as a one-pager.
  5. Copy the Toyota folder structure verbatim; rename and replace content per the eight-step recipe; print-test on A4 landscape before sharing.
  6. Link the one-pager package from 01_account/<Client>_Account_Snapshot.md as the leave-behind for the next CIO/CDO meeting.

16.1 Strategic context

Big Box Store has publicly described a multi-year journey to become a technology-first retailer with proprietary engineering capacity. The company runs its own cloud substrate (Big Box Store Cloud), substantial Azure footprint, and significant on-premises data. Public statements emphasize merchant-in-the-loop AI, supplier collaboration, and associate productivity.

16.2 Public signals (illustrative, verify before pursuit)

  • Announced Azure and OpenAI collaboration for associate-facing tools
  • Ongoing private-cloud strategy balancing Azure + internal
  • Merchant productivity and supplier portal modernization
  • Scale retail media growth
  • Sustainability commitments affecting supplier data exchange

16.3 APEX thesis for Big Box Store

Big Box Store does not need data-platform build help. It needs agent-IP acceleration and semantic-model leverage where its own teams would otherwise invest years. APEX's RC agent library is the wedge. Every engagement positions APEX as co-development framework, not turn-key black box.

16.4 Microsoft pillar lead

Azure AI Foundry — agent orchestration and reasoning at scale. Secondary: Fabric-compatible semantic alignment where Big Box Store data crosses to Azure.

16.5 Priority APEX services

  2. RC-E2E-09 Product Tracking & Traceability (supplier / sustainability)
  3. RC-TTP-07 Markdown Optimization

16.6 Qualifying questions (10)

  1. Which merchant category has the publicly-committed 2026 margin target?
  2. What is the current state of the semantic layer crossing Big Box Store Cloud to Azure?
  3. Which supplier program has the most visible executive attention?
  4. Is there an internal agent-platform already in production?
  5. What is the rollout model — pilot store, banner, geography?
  6. Who is the single-threaded executive owner for the target workload?
  7. What is the incumbent SI on the target scope?
  8. How is ROI measured internally — margin, conversion, associate productivity?
  9. What is the posture on Deloitte IP retention vs client IP ownership?
  10. Independence status — does Deloitte audit this company?

RC-E2E-03 Assortment & Pricing Intelligence — the merchant-facing agent that explains margin exposure by category, with a Copilot experience that makes the recommendations conversational.

16.11 Extended account intelligence

Strategic context beneath the public signals

Big Box Store is engineering-centric by structural choice. They have built their own cloud substrate, their own agent tooling, and internal platform teams that have deeper production AI experience than many SI buy-side teams. The APEX pursuit is therefore positioned as accelerator + reference architecture + delivery muscle — not as a "teach us AI" engagement.

Supplier-program modernization is a specific high-leverage wedge. Big Box Store's supplier scorecards, associate productivity, and sustainability reporting all intersect with the APEX supply-and-provenance services. Entry through the supplier-collaboration angle has a structural advantage: the Big Box Store team responsible is motivated by both top-line (supplier performance) and bottom-line (supplier cost) outcomes.

Competitive landscape on this account

  • Incumbent SIs include Accenture, Infosys, Cognizant, Genpact at scale
  • Big Box Store's own platform teams compete with external SIs for internal reputation
  • Microsoft's Industry Solutions Delivery has direct relationship access
  • AWS has meaningful footprint for specific workloads; Azure is growing

APEX's differentiation on this account is the pre-built RC agent library and the semantic model. Position APEX as what Big Box Store's own engineers would otherwise spend 18–24 months building.

First-90-day detailed playbook

  • Week 1: Independence pre-clearance confirm; identify Merchant, Supply, or Store sponsor
  • Weeks 2–3: Sponsor-led workshop on candidate service scope; coordinate with Microsoft ISD on DCIF if available
  • Weeks 4–8: Wave 1 envisioning (architecture, business case, service selection)
  • Weeks 9–12: Wave 1 close + Wave 2 SOW negotiation

16.12 Scenarios & Use Cases

Scenario 16.12.1: Private-label margin defense (Chief Merchant)

Persona. SVP Private Brands & Sourcing. Owns the Great Value, Member's Mark, Equate, and Mainstays private-label portfolios. Measured on private-label margin percentage and attach rate in managed categories.

Pain. Consumer-packaged-goods suppliers have raised list prices 18–24 % cumulatively over three years; private-label alternative launch velocity has not kept pace. Category managers currently see margin exposure in quarterly review cycles — weeks after the exposure has occurred. Competitive shelf-sets at Target, Kroger, and HEB shift weekly and category teams cannot respond at that cadence.

APEX Solution. RC-E2E-03 Assortment & Pricing Intelligence ingests POS, competitor pricing, and supplier cost data into the Fabric RC semantic model, runs elasticity reasoning on Foundry (o-series for complex categories), and surfaces margin-exposure alerts to category managers through a Teams Copilot card. Every pricing recommendation has a HITL gate where the merchant approves or overrides with reasoning captured. Purview governs supplier-confidential pricing data throughout.

Commercial anchor. RC-E2E-03, Wave 2 lead service. Workstream envelope $3.5–5M of Wave 2 total. Fabric-mirrored supplier and POS data.

Outcome / KPI. Margin uplift of 80–180 basis points in managed categories within 12 months; category-manager decision cycle from quarterly to 48 hours. Each dollar of margin protected traces to a specific merchant decision in the audit row.

Scenario 16.12.2: Supplier-collaboration modernization (Chief Merchandising Officer / Supply Chain)

Persona. SVP Supplier Development. Owns the Retail Link supplier interface, supplier scorecards, and supplier-collaboration programs across 100,000+ suppliers worldwide.

Pain. Retail Link reporting is self-service but cognitively dense; suppliers complain they cannot identify which of their SKUs are underperforming until scorecard cycles. Big Box Store's internal supplier-development team manually triages the top 500 suppliers and leaves the long tail to self-service. Fraud and performance issues in the long tail surface late.

APEX Solution. RC-E2E-Supplier-Intelligence ingests supplier performance, chargeback, and shipment-compliance data into Fabric; Foundry agents rank supplier anomalies across the full portfolio; Copilot Studio surfaces prioritized supplier outreach recommendations to the supplier-development team. For suppliers, a Copilot Studio self-service surface answers scorecard questions in natural language grounded on Retail Link data.

Commercial anchor. RC-E2E-Supplier services suite, Wave 2. Workstream envelope $4–6M. Draws heavily on Azure Databricks where Big Box Store already ingests Retail Link data (see Appendix F for co-existence pattern).

Outcome / KPI. Supplier-development team covers the full tail, not just top 500; chargeback recovery up 15–25 %; supplier NPS measurable uplift. Audit row attributes recovered chargebacks to specific supplier-development actions.

Scenario 16.12.3: Associate productivity in the back-room (COO / Chief Stores)

Persona. VP Store Operations. Responsible for in-store associate productivity, task-management cadence, and back-room throughput across 4,700+ US stores.

Pain. Associates receive tasks through the Me@Big Box Store app, but task prioritisation is store-manager-driven and inconsistent. On a given shift, the associate performs tasks in the order set by the manager at open; if the day changes (weather, truck delay, BOPIS surge), the task order is stale by noon. Re-prioritisation is manual and interrupts the manager's own work.

APEX Solution. RC-E2E-07 Store Operations Intelligence ingests task completion, POS, inventory, shrink-event, and labor-schedule data into Fabric Eventstream. Foundry agents re-sequence task queues as conditions change; the associate's Me@Big Box Store app surfaces the updated task list with a one-line reason ("re-prioritized due to BOPIS surge — fulfillment tasks moved up"). Managers approve re-prioritisation patterns through a Teams Copilot HITL gate at the pattern level, not per-task.

Commercial anchor. RC-E2E-07, Wave 2 or Wave 3 depending on pilot scale. Workstream envelope $2–4M Wave 2 pilot; $8–15M Wave 3 enterprise. Microsoft 365 Copilot surface.

Outcome / KPI. Task completion rate up 8–15 %; associate time-per-task down 10–20 %; manager re-prioritisation workload down 60–80 %. Every re-prioritisation traces to a condition change in the audit row.

Scenario 16.12.4: Sustainability-program provenance defensibility (Chief Sustainability Officer)

Persona. SVP Sustainability. Accountable for Project Gigaton, Scope 3 disclosure, and the sustainability attestations underlying private-label claims.

Pain. Project Gigaton reporting requires supplier emissions data at SKU level; supplier self-reporting is inconsistent and audit-indefensible. California SB-253 and SEC climate rules add legal exposure on top of reputational exposure. When a journalist or activist challenges a specific product claim, the evidence trail is a manual reconstruction across multiple tools.

APEX Solution. RC-E2E-09 Product Tracking & Traceability ingests supplier submissions, lot-level manufacturing data, and third-party verification feeds into Fabric. Purview applies classification and lineage throughout. Foundry agents score supplier submissions for anomalies; Copilot surfaces attestation evidence packages to sustainability and legal teams on demand. The audit row constitutes the regulator-ready evidence chain.

Commercial anchor. RC-E2E-09, Wave 2 extension. Workstream envelope $2.5–4M. Purview-heavy (35 % of effort).

Outcome / KPI. Journalist / regulator queries answered in hours, not weeks; attestation defensibility qualitatively strong; Scope 3 disclosure prepared with auditable evidence. Audit row provides the lineage from supplier submission to public claim.

Scenario 16.12.5: BOPIS accuracy and substitution (VP Digital Fulfilment)

Persona. VP Digital Fulfilment & Last Mile. Owns BOPIS, curbside pickup, and home-delivery fulfillment across store and last-mile network.

Pain. BOPIS substitution rates vary 8–22 % across stores; customer NPS on substitutions is 30+ points below non-substituted orders. Associates make substitution choices with limited customer-preference context. The customer-communication surface is a templated SMS that lacks personalisation.

APEX Solution. RC-E2E-BPX-06 (BOPIS Substitution) detects stock-exception mid-pick, queries RC-E2E-05 Unified Customer Intelligence for member preferences, and surfaces a recommended substitution to the associate through Me@Big Box Store. A Copilot Studio surface generates the customer outreach with personalised language; the customer can respond in natural language and the associate sees the response. HITL throughout — associate confirms every substitution.

Commercial anchor. RC-E2E-BPX-06 + RC-E2E-05 integration, Wave 2. Workstream envelope $3–5M. Copilot Studio heavy.

Outcome / KPI. Substitution NPS gap closes 15–20 points; member retention on substituted orders up 5–10 %; associate substitution decision time down 40–60 %. Audit row attributes member retention to specific substitution decisions.

Scenario 16.12.6: Store-closure decisioning with CFO attribution (CFO / VP Real Estate)

Persona. VP Real Estate Strategy and partner at the CFO office. Responsible for store-network optimization, including closure decisions in under-performing markets.

Pain. Store-closure proposals flow through a committee process with multi-quarter evaluation cycles. The financial model is rigorous but slow; scenario exploration ("what if we convert to Neighborhood Market?", "what if we sublet 30 % of the footprint?") is manually modeled by a small team. Decision inputs are stale by the time the committee meets.

APEX Solution. RC-E2E-RealEstate Intelligence ingests sales, labor, real-estate costs, demographic trends, competitive density, and e-commerce substitution data into Fabric. Foundry agents run scenario-permutation analysis and surface ranked options to the real-estate team through Power BI Direct Lake + a Copilot scenario-exploration surface. Every scenario carries the input assumptions and the attribution model, enabling CFO-credible defensibility.

Commercial anchor. RC-E2E-RealEstate, Wave 2 or Wave 3. Workstream envelope $1.5–3M.

Outcome / KPI. Closure-decision cycle from 2 quarters to 4–6 weeks; committee decision confidence rises; post-closure financial performance matches pre-closure projection within 5 % (attribution-defensible). Every committee decision traces to specific scenario inputs in the audit row.

Scenario 16.12.7: Multi-cloud coexistence with Big Box Store Cloud and Azure Databricks (CTO)

Persona. SVP Platform Engineering. Responsible for Big Box Store's internal cloud substrate and for the boundary with Azure and AWS workloads.

Pain. Big Box Store runs a proprietary cloud plus significant Azure and AWS. Big Box Store's own engineering teams have built substantial AI tooling, and their relationship with external SI proposals is sceptical. Any APEX proposal must explicitly respect what Big Box Store has already built; otherwise the platform team blocks the commercial.

APEX Solution. APEX enters as reference architecture plus delivery muscle, not black-box platform. Fabric serves the APEX workload specifically; OneLake shortcuts reach Big Box Store Cloud and Azure Databricks data in place (Databricks co-existence pattern from Appendix F). Big Box Store's own engineers extend the APEX agent library; Deloitte's role is Wave 1 envisioning and Wave 2 implementation acceleration. IP retained by Deloitte is framework-level; everything in Big Box Store's tenant is Big Box Store's.

Commercial anchor. Applies across Wave 1 and Wave 2 as an architectural principle, not a separate workstream.

Outcome / KPI. Platform-team acceptance of APEX; time-to-first-production-service 9–12 months vs the 18–24 months Big Box Store engineers would otherwise need; clean exit path preserved throughout.

Scenario 16.12.8: Wave 3 expansion into Neighborhood Market (Wave 3 lead)

Persona. President, US Neighborhood Market (or equivalent segment head). Owns the ~800-store Neighborhood Market footprint distinct from Supercenter.

Pain. Neighborhood Market has a different unit economics profile (smaller basket, higher trip frequency, more grocery-weighted) than Supercenter; services tuned for Supercenter do not automatically work in NM. Without deliberate extension, Wave 2 value captured in Supercenter does not translate.

APEX Solution. Wave 3 extension program takes the RC service catalog proven in Supercenter Wave 2 and retunes for Neighborhood Market unit economics. The semantic model, agent library, and governance carry over; model parameters, HITL gates, and KPI targets re-tune. Wave 3 commercial envelope reflects extension, not rebuild.

Commercial anchor. Wave 3 extension across the catalog. Envelope $8–18M over 18–24 months. Microsoft Fabric capacity scales with unit count.

Outcome / KPI. NM deployment time 40–60 % faster than Supercenter Wave 2 (pattern reuse); NM margin uplift comparable to Supercenter (scaled for basket size); Big Box Store AI program-wide ROI visibility consolidated.

16.13.2 Event 01 — Reefer 14 was warm for four hours (5:58 AM, Cold Chain)

Situation. Between 02:15 and 06:27 the dairy endcap held at 48–52 °F against a 41 °F threshold. By the time Marisol swiped in at 5:58 AM the refrigeration case had been cooling back for twenty minutes — and her phone already held a disposition-ready brief on the affected inventory.

Agents at work. Cold-chain telemetry agents consumed 252 sensor readings from the reefer unit (Fabric Eventhouse). A correlation agent on Foundry joined temperature excursion to the 28 affected SKUs and 412 units at risk. FDA food-safety thresholds by sub-category split the inventory into save-viable (vacuum-sealed, low-risk) vs destroy (ready-to-eat dairy, soft cheese). A quarantine task was assigned to a pull-team lead; case labels were pre-printed at the service desk. A write-off pre-approval with telemetry attached was routed to Marisol's Teams Copilot for a single-tap approval. The refrigeration vendor was ticketed automatically — root cause tracked to compressor soft-start failure via ADX time-series.

Marisol's HITL decision (6:08 AM). "Confirm save/destroy after visual inspection. Approve $534 targeted write-off."

Outcome. 71 % of inventory saved. $1,313 write-off avoided against a $1,847 exposure. Doors opened at 7:00 with the dairy endcap re-fronted. Time-to-brief: 8 minutes. Manager touch: 90 seconds. Audit trail: complete.

How Deloitte delivered this. Fabric Eventstream + Eventhouse ingested the telemetry; Foundry agents (designed using APEX agent library patterns) performed the correlation and disposition; Teams Copilot Studio surface rendered the HITL card; Purview classified the inventory-loss evidence chain; audit row attributes the $1,313 to this specific decision.

16.13.3 Event 02 — DSD discrepancy at the receiving dock (7:20 AM, Receiving)

Situation. An RFID portal scan on the inbound dock clocked four cases short of the invoice — the rep said 48, the portal read 44. Before the rep reached the back office the agent had built the dispute package, including the pattern: three short-ships from this vendor in ninety days.

Agents at work. The receiving event streamed from the UHF RFID portal into Fabric. An agent reconciled the actual count against ASN line-level detail and confirmed the variance was in the 12oz multipack specifically. A second agent pulled 90-day vendor history — three prior short-ships, $487 in previously-disputed-unresolved claims. A dispute-claim draft was generated with portal logs and dock-camera frame references. The "sign disputed" receipt was pre-filled for the rep's iPad.

Marisol's HITL decision (7:24 AM). "Sign disputed. Let the claim run. Flag vendor for category manager escalation if the pattern hits four."

Outcome. $142.56 claim filed with timestamped evidence before the truck left the lot. Historically this reconciliation happened a week later, post-invoice, with weak evidence. Now it happens at the dock. Evidence quality: strong. Manager touch: 45 seconds. Vendor pattern: 3 of last 90 days.

16.13.4 Event 03 — Stale tags on the pet aisle (8:36 AM, Price Integrity)

Situation. The ESL gateway silently dropped an overnight push. Shelf showed regular price. POS rang promotional. By the fourth transaction the agent had caught the gap, frozen the loss, and staged the fix.

Agents at work. POS transaction streams in Fabric Eventhouse. A price-integrity agent detected promo-vs-shelf divergence on the fourth ring at 08:34:12. The stale override was suspended at the register; POS now rang the scheduled regular price, keeping compliance posture intact. A paper-tag print job for the 127 affected SKUs was queued at the service desk printer to bridge until ESL recovered. The ESL gateway vendor was ticketed; cause: firmware handshake after a software update the prior evening.

Marisol's HITL decision (8:41 AM). "Print the tags, walk the aisle, get the vendor on the phone."

Outcome. Loss frozen in four rings. 127 SKUs remediated with paper tags within 40 minutes; ESL restored that afternoon. Margin erosion from stale promo: contained to four transactions. Manager touch: 2 minutes.

16.13.5 Event 04 — Phantom OOS on 18 high-velocity SKUs (10:15 AM, OSA Triage)

Situation. Computer vision, POS velocity, and perpetual inventory agreed: eighteen high-velocity SKUs were selling through to zero at shelf while backroom said otherwise. The agent sorted the pick list by velocity and handed it to the most-available associate — no manager debate needed.

Agents at work. Shelf-camera CV + 4-hour rolling POS velocity + perpetual inventory position fused in Fabric. An OSA agent confirmed all 18 empty facings with 312 units of backroom stock available. A planogram lookup generated aisle-by-aisle pick locations sorted by velocity. The task was assigned to associate Marcus R. based on current zone, radio status, and last-task completion time — his handheld received the pick list.

Marisol's decision (10:16 AM). "Seen. Go." (Acknowledge only — no HITL required for this routine remediation.)

Outcome. 18 facings restocked in 34 minutes. No manager walk; no category-team call. Sales protected: ~$2,100. Historically this class of event was detected by store-walk or customer complaint and resolved in hours-to-days. Manager touch: 5 seconds.

16.13.6 Event 05 — FDA Class II infant-formula recall (11:45 AM, Recall Impact)

Situation. An FDA Class II recall posted at 11:43 on a specific lot of infant formula. The recall agent resolved the entire FSMA 204 chain before the notification tone on Marisol's phone finished — 87 units on shelf, 32 sold in 14 days, 29 loyalty customers to notify.

Agents at work. Within 4 minutes of FDA post: the recall agent resolved upstream lot-trace to vendor, shipment, and receiving events at Store 100. Exposure quantified: 87 on shelf, 121 backroom, 32 sold (29 loyalty-identified, 3 anonymous tender). A pull-from-shelf task was generated for two associates; quarantine bay QB-03 was designated. A bilingual customer notification (email + SMS) with prepaid return label and full refund was drafted — held for manager release. A regulatory hold was posted to the POS so any remaining units scanned at register blocked the sale.

Marisol's HITL decision (11:49 AM). "Release the customer notifications — I'll oversee the floor pull myself. Get me Corporate Comms on the line before we send."

Outcome. 208 units pulled and quarantined in 22 minutes. 29 customers reached within one hour of the FDA post. Full FSMA 204 traceability trail preserved as an auditable artifact. Benchmark equivalent events historically took 4–6 hours just to scope.

16.13.7 Event 06 — BOPIS substitution (12:32 PM, Customer Experience)

Situation. A BOPIS picker hit an empty shelf on an organic spinach SKU for customer Jennifer's order. Forty-seven seconds later the customer had tapped an accept on the proposed substitute. This event illustrates what fully-autonomous CX looks like — no manager surface, full-loop closed.

Agents at work. The pick exception triggered a substitution agent that retrieved Jennifer's 14-month substitution acceptance history — she accepts conventional when organic is out, rejects size upsizes. Three candidate SKUs were ranked by predicted acceptance; the top pick was sent via SMS with one-tap confirm. Jennifer confirmed in 47 seconds; picker notified to complete; fulfillment status advanced.

No HITL required. Fully autonomous. Surfaces to the manager only if the customer rejects all options or an aging threshold trips.

Outcome. Order fulfilled on the original pickup slot. Customer satisfaction preserved. Manager shield intact — this is the class of event that silently consumes the majority of an associate-floor lead's day in the pre-agent world. Resolution: 47 seconds. Manager touch: 0.

16.13.8 Event 07 — Shrink pattern on register 7 (1:47 PM, Shrink Signal)

Situation. A 72-hour pattern tripped the shrink signal: register 7, one associate, an anomalous void cadence on high-value spirits, no matching return receipts, and a matching inventory variance downstream. Not an accusation — an evidence package.

Agents at work. A shrink-signal agent correlated POS void pattern (4.2× normal rate on spirits), inventory variance (-7 units, category match), schedule (3-of-3 days), and absence of matching return receipts across 72 hours. Confidence band computed; surfacing was suppressed until the pattern crossed the 3σ threshold. Evidence timeline assembled with CCTV frame references (not footage — timestamps AP needs to pull). Case held behind an AP-only surface; the associate and supervisor were not notified directly.

Marisol's HITL decision (1:54 PM). "Escalate to AP with the package. No conversation with the associate from me. Handle this the right way."

Outcome. AP investigation opened with a clean, statistically-grounded evidence package. Manager stays out of the direct line of inquiry — protecting the investigation and the associate's due process. Pattern confidence: 3.1σ. Evidence rows: 41. Manager touch: 2 minutes.

16.13.9 Event 08 — Foreign object in a sealed muffin (2:33 PM, Customer Incident)

Situation. A customer came to the service desk with a photo and a sealed package. The agent pulled the lot code from the photo, traced it to a specific co-manufacturer bakery run, and surfaced two prior low-severity complaints on the same lot at other stores. What looked like a one-store incident was actually the third signal of something systemic.

Agents at work. An OCR agent extracted lot code B-2841 from the customer's phone photo; confirmed against product master. The lot was resolved to Northwind Bakery (co-manufacturer); identified shared lot across 14 stores. A cross-match against open customer-incident cases found 2 prior low-severity complaints on the same lot — emerging pattern. A Tier 2 case was opened; QA + Legal + Corporate Comms notified in parallel; evidence-preservation protocol initiated. The agent recommended proactive pull at the 13 other affected stores before additional complaints landed.

Marisol's HITL decision (2:39 PM). "Full refund plus a gift card to the customer. Preserve the package. Get me the QA lead — we have to pull this lot from all fourteen stores tonight."

Outcome. Full case file assembled in 6 minutes — historically 45+ minutes of manual lot-trace work. More importantly: pattern detection enabled a proactive pull at 13 other stores before additional complaints landed. What began as a local incident became an enterprise-level quality signal. Legal posture: evidence preserved.

Foundry agents score requests in real time; high-risk requests route through additional verification before fulfillment. HITL for policy tuning by SNKRS team, not per-request. Purview governs behavioral signals with appropriate classification.

Commercial anchor. RC-TTP-Launch Integrity, Wave 2. Workstream envelope $2–4M. Fabric Real-Time Intelligence heavy.

Outcome / KPI. Authentic-member purchase share on high-demand drops up 15–30 percentage points; re-sell listing velocity down 25–40 %; enthusiast NPS on launches improves measurably.

Pain. Inventory levels rose during 2022–2023; normalisation continues through 2026. Markdown cadence is the lever but is applied inconsistently across regions and categories. Margin erosion on markdown is 200–400 basis points worse than plan in managed categories.

APEX Solution. RC-TTP-07 Markdown Optimization scores sell-through probability at SKU-store-day level using Foundry reasoning on Fabric-resident inventory, POS, seasonal-pattern, and competitor data. 20.12 Scenarios & Use Cases

Scenario 20.12.1: Generative engineering for next-vehicle program (Chief Engineer)

Persona. Chief Engineer, specific vehicle program (e.g., next-generation EV truck platform). Accountable for engineering milestone delivery.

Pain. Design-space exploration for structural, thermal, and aerodynamic optimization runs through traditional CAD / CAE loops with simulation bottlenecks. Time-to-first-viable-design on a new program is the critical-path constraint. Competitive pressure from Tesla, Rivian, and Chinese OEMs compresses the schedule.

APEX Solution. AXLE-E2E-Product-03 Generative Engineering Assistant orchestrates Ansys / Siemens NX / Altair simulation sweeps with Foundry agents that explore the design space within engineering-grade constraints. Each candidate carries provenance (model, seed, constraints, feasibility checks). Chief Engineer's team reviews ranked candidates through a Copilot-grounded engineering review surface. Manufacturing-feasibility agent pre-screens.

Commercial anchor. AXLE-E2E-Product-03, Wave 2 lead. Workstream envelope $6–10M. Reasoning-tier Foundry consumption elevated.

Outcome / KPI. Design-space exploration cycle cut 40–60 %; time-to-first-viable-design compressed materially; engineering-team leverage on experienced chief engineers.

Scenario 20.12.2: Connected factory OEE (Chief Manufacturing Officer)

Persona. Chief Manufacturing Officer. Accountable for plant-level OEE, quality, and unplanned-downtime performance across the assembly and powertrain plant network.

Pain. OEE variance plant-to-plant is wide. Unplanned downtime events disrupt schedules with cascading supply effects. Root-cause analysis on quality events runs on weekly cadence; faster response is operationally possible but analytically constrained.

APEX Solution. AXLE-E2E-Manufacturing-02 Connected Factory ingests MES (Plex), quality systems, maintenance history, and historian data into Fabric. Foundry agents correlate in near-real-time; Copilot surfaces prioritized alerts to plant supervisors. HITL for root-cause confirmation; audit row captures reasoning.

Commercial anchor. AXLE-E2E-Manufacturing-02, Wave 2. Workstream envelope $5–8M per lead plant.

Outcome / KPI. OEE uplift 3–7 percentage points in lead plants; unplanned downtime down 15–25 %; root-cause cycle from days to hours.

Scenario 20.12.3: Warranty cost prevention (VP Aftermarket / Warranty)

Persona. VP Global Warranty. Responsible for warranty cost containment across current and prior model years.

Pain. Warranty claims are processed through dealer networks; field-failure patterns emerge weeks or months after the leading-edge claims surface. Root-cause attribution to supplier components vs design choices vs operator behavior is complex. Warranty reserves are informed by lagging data.

APEX Solution. AXLE-TTP-Quality ingests warranty claim, dealer-service, supplier-component, and in-service telematics into Fabric. Foundry agents pattern-match emerging failure signatures. Copilot Studio surfaces findings to warranty-engineering team with proposed root-cause hypotheses. Supplier recovery cycles tightened.

Commercial anchor. AXLE-TTP-Quality, Wave 2. Workstream envelope $3–5M. Value-share commercial applicable to supplier recovery.

Outcome / KPI. Field-failure pattern detection from months to days; supplier recovery rate up 15–25 %; warranty reserve accuracy improved.

Scenario 20.12.4: Ultifi / SDV data platform enablement (Chief Digital Officer / SDV)

Persona. Chief Digital Officer, Software-Defined Vehicle. Owns Ultifi platform trajectory and connected-vehicle data monetisation.

Pain. Connected-vehicle data at GM scale is enormous; extracting business value requires agent-platform maturity beyond current state. Subscription-service product decisions depend on behavioral insight; insight depends on data + reasoning infrastructure.

APEX Solution. APEX services consume Ultifi telemetry through Fabric Eventhouse; Foundry agents produce subscription-service-relevant behavioral insights; governance under Purview with consumer-privacy protections. SDV product team uses Copilot-grounded surfaces for feature-evaluation analytics.

Commercial anchor. Wave 2 or Wave 3 extension. Workstream envelope $5–10M.

Outcome / KPI. SDV team feature-evaluation cycle accelerated; subscription-feature uptake insight improves; monetisation trajectory supported.

Scenario 20.12.5: Predictive service for commercial vehicles (VP Service Operations)

Persona. VP Service Operations, Commercial Trucks. Responsible for dealer-service network performance for commercial customers with uptime-sensitive fleets.

Pain. Commercial customer uptime expectations are uncompromising; breakdowns carry downstream business impact far exceeding the repair cost. Predictive service is nominally available but under-utilized; dealers vary in their adoption.

APEX Solution. AXLE-E2E-Aftermarket-02 Predictive Service ingests vehicle telematics and service history into Fabric. Foundry agents generate service recommendations per vehicle; Copilot Studio surfaces to dealers and fleet customers. HITL for dealer acceptance of recommendations.

Commercial anchor. AXLE-E2E-Aftermarket-02, Wave 2 or Wave 3. Workstream envelope $3–5M.

Outcome / KPI. Commercial-customer uptime up; dealer-service revenue from predictive program grows; customer NPS on commercial fleets improves.

Scenario 20.12.6: Safety-assurance-sensitive program scoping (VP Vehicle Safety)

Persona. VP Vehicle Safety & Homologation. Responsible for safety-critical design review and regulatory homologation.

Pain. AI-assisted design or operational decisions in safety-critical domains carry incremental assurance burden. Engineering teams want AI leverage but safety review cannot be shortcut.

APEX Solution. APEX safety-sensitive workflows route through dedicated safety-assurance QR before service deployment. HITL gates are explicit; automation is conservative. Safety review becomes a scheduled activity with known cost and timeline rather than an unbounded risk.

Commercial anchor. Applies to specific services; safety-assurance QR adds 15–25 % to workstream timeline and cost.

Outcome / KPI. Safety-reviewed services deploy on predictable timelines; Chief Engineer confidence in AI programs maintained; regulator posture strong.

Scenario 20.12.7: Independence-compliant delivery (audit-client-specific)

Persona. CIO in partnership with General Counsel and Audit Committee liaison.

Pain. As a Deloitte audit client, GM engagements require Audit Committee pre-clearance and specific scope definitions. Commercial friction if not handled cleanly.

APEX Solution. APEX scope categories pre-cleared; funding paths (direct / DCIF / ISV / SI teaming) only; ECIF declined. Ongoing Independence reporting through the engagement lifecycle. Audit Committee liaison maintained.

Commercial anchor. Operational discipline; affects envelope predictability, not commercial structure.

Outcome / KPI. Zero Independence findings; scope expansion viable within cleared categories; Audit Committee confident in engagement management.

Scenario 20.12.8: CFO attribution across SDV + Manufacturing + Aftermarket (CFO)

Persona. CFO. Allocating capital across SDV / software, manufacturing transformation, and aftermarket programs.

Pain. Benefit attribution across these large program categories is imprecise. AI-program capital requests compete with other uses; board scrutiny on AI ROI is active.

APEX Solution. APEX audit-row pattern provides per-service dollar attribution across all three program categories. CFO's FP&A team can query attribution at the program, service, and decision level. Board-level AI-spend reporting becomes specific.

Commercial anchor. Cross-service; enabled by the audit-row pattern foundational to APEX.

Outcome / KPI. CFO-credible AI attribution per program; board-level ROI reporting specific; capital-allocation confidence improves.

26.12 Scenarios & Use Cases

Scenario 26.12.1: IROPs disruption recovery (COO)

Persona. Chief Operations Officer. Accountable for operational reliability across hub networks.

Pain. Irregular operations (weather, mechanical, crew) cascade through hub networks. Re-accommodation decisions affect thousands of passengers per event; decision quality affects customer satisfaction, regulatory exposure (DOT tarmac rules), and operational recovery speed.

APEX Solution. TH-E2E-Air-01 Disruption Recovery ingests flight-ops, crew availability, passenger-itinerary, partner-airline-space, and ground-services data into Fabric Eventhouse. Foundry agents produce re-accommodation plans; Copilot Studio surfaces options to ops-controllers and gate-agents with rationale. HITL for controller approval. Audit row captures every re-accommodation.

Commercial anchor. TH-E2E-Air-01, Wave 2 lead. Workstream envelope $5–8M. Fabric Real-Time Intelligence heavy.

Outcome / KPI. Re-accommodation cycle compressed; passenger NPS during IROPs improves; DOT-tarmac compliance strong; operational-recovery time down.

Scenario 26.12.2: Traveler profile resolution (Chief Digital Officer)

Persona. Chief Digital Officer. Owns digital experience and the traveler-identity problem across reservation, loyalty, and ops systems.

Pain. A traveler is represented multiple times across Sabre PSS, AAdvantage loyalty, revenue-management, and operational systems. Consistent personalisation and cross-journey context are limited.

APEX Solution. TH-TTP-07 Traveler Profile & Preferences resolves identity across PSS, loyalty, and ops systems into a unified traveler graph in Fabric. Foundry agents produce traveler-context surfaces; Copilot and Copilot Studio expose context to gate agents, airport managers, and customer-care.

Commercial anchor. TH-TTP-07, Wave 2. Workstream envelope $4–6M.

Outcome / KPI. Traveler-context completeness up measurably; gate-agent effectiveness up; personalised outreach during IROPs improves.

Scenario 26.12.3: AAdvantage loyalty economics (SVP Loyalty)

Persona. SVP Loyalty & Customer. Accountable for AAdvantage program economics and growth.

Pain. Loyalty program growth depends on earn-burn balance, partner-economics tuning, and member engagement. Cross-partner data (co-brand card, airline-partner earnings, retail-partner redemptions) is fragmented.

APEX Solution. TH-TTP-Loyalty ingests AAdvantage activity, partner earnings, member behavior into Fabric. Foundry agents produce member-value analytics and program-economic simulations. Copilot surfaces to loyalty team.

Commercial anchor. TH-TTP-Loyalty, Wave 2. Workstream envelope $3–5M.

Outcome / KPI. Loyalty-program unit economics improve; member-value-per-cohort trending up; program-level NPS lift.

Scenario 26.12.4: Distribution-strategy analytics (Chief Commercial Officer)

Persona. Chief Commercial Officer. Responsible for distribution mix and NDC adoption strategy.

Pain. Distribution strategy (NDC vs EDIFACT vs direct) is in transition across TH industry. Channel-by-channel economics and sales-behavior insights inform strategy but lag.

APEX Solution. TH-TTP-Distribution ingests booking-channel data, NDC adoption metrics, fare-shopping patterns into Fabric. Foundry agents produce channel-economic insights. Copilot surfaces to distribution strategy team.

Commercial anchor. TH-TTP-Distribution, Wave 2 extension. Workstream envelope $1.5–3M.

Outcome / KPI. Distribution-strategy decision latency down; NDC-adoption measurable progress; channel-mix optimization.

Scenario 26.12.5: Crew-operations Copilot (VP Crew Scheduling)

Persona. VP Crew Scheduling & Operations. Responsible for crew resource management, bidding, and re-assignment.

Pain. Crew operations is union-governed and highly regulated. Crew-scheduler workflow involves complex rule application under time pressure during IROPs.

APEX Solution. TH-E2E-Air-02 Crew & Airport Ops Copilot surfaces crew rule application, crew-availability, and re-assignment options to scheduler within union contract constraints. HITL throughout — scheduler decides within contractually-scoped options.

Commercial anchor. TH-E2E-Air-02, Wave 2. Workstream envelope $2–4M.

Outcome / KPI. Scheduler productivity up; IROPs recovery time with correct crew assignments improves; union-contract compliance strong.

Scenario 26.12.6: Gate-agent customer service (Airport Operations leadership)

Persona. VP Airport Operations. Responsible for airport-level customer-experience and gate-agent productivity.

Pain. Gate agents work under time pressure with passenger-facing complexity. Information tools have improved but multi-system coordination at gate remains manual.

APEX Solution. Gate-agent Copilot surface consolidates relevant passenger, flight, partner-airline-space, and policy data; gate-agent sees recommended actions for re-bookings and passenger service. HITL throughout.

Commercial anchor. Extension of TH-TTP-07 + TH-E2E-Air-01. Workstream envelope $2–3M.

Outcome / KPI. Passenger-wait at gate reduced; gate-agent first-resolution rate up; passenger-NPS during disruption improves.

Persona. CIO in partnership with Audit Committee liaison.

Pain. Applicable if AAL is a Deloitte audit client — pre-clearance, scope boundaries, ongoing Independence reporting.

APEX Solution. Pre-clearance secured; scope categories explicit; funding paths compliant; Independence-Office liaison continuous.

Commercial anchor. Operational discipline.

Outcome / KPI. Zero findings; engagement viability maintained.

Scenario 26.12.8: Safety-assurance-sensitive workflow boundary (Chief Safety Officer)

Persona. Chief Safety Officer. Owns safety-assurance reviews for anything touching flight operations.

Pain. Any AI-adjacent tool entering flight-operations territory requires safety review. Scope discipline matters.
